# omx-dsp / fuzz_delay

omx-dsp's own fuzz target `fuzz_delay` ([source](source/fuzz_delay.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-dsp 0.27.0 (FreeMixer/omx-dsp at a0ee1dfe).

Reads a flags byte and a ring size of 1 to 4096. The fractional mode arms a Lagrange delay line of order 3, order 5 or any signed byte, and runs up to 12 finite blocks, each with any float delay. The integer mode runs up to 12 blocks of a stereo or mono integer delay pair, with delays in tenths of a millisecond at a declared rate. It can also check the ms-to-samples conversion for any finite ms and rate. The harness keeps its own copy of the take as the oracle.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libomxdsp.a, which build.sh compiles from omx-dsp's five src/*.c files with -DOMX_CONTRACTS and -ffp-contract=off; both delay lines are inline in the headers. The Makefile's own fuzz build uses native clang with libFuzzer, which this build replaces with the standard driver.
- omx-contract's headers are pinned to the tag v3.4.0 (1169c701), where the library's Makefile uses whichever omx-contract is installed, at or above its packaging floor of 3.1.0.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A ring takes a line exactly when the order is 3 or 5 and the ring is longer than the kernel's reach. A refusal returns the code that names its cause and leaves the line unarmed ([lines 99-134](source/fuzz_delay.c#L99-L134)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An unarmed line reports a latency of 0 and leaves the block unchanged, bit for bit ([lines 150-165](source/fuzz_delay.c#L150-L165)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The delay delivered is finite and inside the ring's longest delay, and a non-finite request reads as 0. The delay also equals the harness's own reading of the rule in the library's comment ([lines 170-192](source/fuzz_delay.c#L170-L192)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every sample from the fractional line is finite and no larger than the absolute sum of the Lagrange weights times the take's peak ([lines 202-215](source/fuzz_delay.c#L202-L215)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A whole-sample delay outputs the take delayed by that many samples, bit for bit, with zero before the take starts ([lines 218-226](source/fuzz_delay.c#L218-L226)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A fractional delay outputs the Lagrange sum, computed by the harness over its copy of the take, to within a tolerance scaled by the weights and the peak ([lines 232-238](source/fuzz_delay.c#L232-L238)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- omx_idelay_samples is inside the ring. It is the rounded delay saturated at the ring's last slot, and 0 for a delay of no length. This holds both for any finite ms and rate and for the grid's ms and declared rates ([lines 261-302](source/fuzz_delay.c#L261-L302)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A steady integer delay on either leg outputs the take delayed, bit for bit ([lines 318-347](source/fuzz_delay.c#L318-L347)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- While the integer delay moves, each sample on either leg stays between the old tap and the new tap it fades across ([lines 329-356](source/fuzz_delay.c#L329-L356)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- At the end of the input, no contract of the library is recorded as broken. The ledger is emptied after the calls whose PRE the harness breaks on purpose ([lines 160-168](source/fuzz.h#L160-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.
